mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in FEDFUNDS (current value below 2%) predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days (always active).
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year window, or 20-day returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in UNRATE above 6.0% triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p < 0.05) when UNRATE crosses above 6.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in GDPC1 (demand) and HOUST (demand) amplifies positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns not significantly positive when both proxies rise concurrently (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rising > 0.5% over 3 months), rising FEDFUNDS predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day returns not significantly negative (t-test p < 0.05) during an identified tightening cycle.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in INDPRO (supply) predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days (always active).
failure_condition: 60-day returns not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) despite rising INDPRO.

mechanism_narrative: A drop in PAYEMS below 144,000 employees triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: 5-day returns not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when PAYEMS crosses below 144,000.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent growth in GDPC1 (demand) and RSAFS (demand) predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns not significantly positive when both proxies rise concurrently (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a contractionary labor market (UNRATE below 5%), rising UNRATE predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day returns not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during contractionary labor markets when UNRATE crosses above 5%.
